# Review: 200-dataset experimental specification

**Summary verdict: REVISE AND RESUBMIT.** The overall design is sound: one biological truth per design, paired platform simulation, design-level split, sealed final panel, predeclared gates, six families. But five pre-generation decisions are either uncalibrated, unrealizable with the declared tooling, or leak the final truth. These must be fixed before any seed is consumed, because splits, seeds, and structure files cannot be changed afterward without a new panel. I read the spec, the v0.11.0 code, the prior audits, and the MucOneUp 0.44.5 source that the spec pins. I did not open the existing response file in `.planning/reviews/checkpoint1_spec/` so that this review stays independent. This session is read-only, so nothing was written to `.planning/`.

## Detailed findings

**C1, CRITICAL. Section 3.1, lines 90 to 104. Absolute gates are calibrated to a different panel.** The baselines cited (10/44, 40/44, 24/28, 14 extras) come from the historical 44-sample HiFi set, which was mostly 200-template, typical-gap, dupC-heavy. The new dev panel deliberately adds 7 identical, 14 gap-1 to 3, 10 extreme-asymmetry, 8 length-extreme, and a low-coverage tier. The v0.11.0 baseline on that panel will be far below 90.9% count pairs, so "≥92%" is neither a delta nor a calibrated absolute. Remedy: make step 1 of the protocol "run frozen v0.11.0 on all 140 dev datasets and record per-design outcomes". Then restate every gate as a paired delta on the same panel with the baseline value filled in from that run, plus a no-regression rule (zero previously exact pairs lost, zero new normal alarms). Keep the absolute numbers only as secondary "aspiration" values. Also state denominators per platform: HiFi gates use 70 designs, ONT gates use 70 designs, never "140 datasets".

**C2, CRITICAL. Sections 2.2 and 5, lines 47 and 144 to 151. The blinding protocol leaks the final truth.** MucOneUp is deterministic given config and seed, and PCR allocation is deterministic by default. Publishing `bio_seed` in an append-only ledger visible to development agents is equivalent to publishing the final truth, since anyone can rerun `simulate`. Second leak: the maintained runner writes reads and truth FASTA into the same case directory and the inventory records `truth_dir`, and the generation manifest embeds the full design JSON. Third leak: if neutral tokens are assigned in design-table order, `sample_val_001..010` are the controls. Remedy: (a) split the ledger into a public execution ledger (token, platform, input hash, status, timings) and a sealed truth ledger (seeds, lengths, mutation, truth hashes, per-allele support) with a published SHA-256 commitment of the sealed file; (b) create a caller-facing directory containing only renamed read files, with the token mapping sealed; (c) assign tokens by a seeded random permutation recorded in the sealed ledger; (d) name the validation executor and give it a script that verifies hashes and emits only aggregate pass/fail.

**C3, CRITICAL. Section 2.3, rows "Equal Lengths (Identical)" and "Repeat Composition". These strata are not producible with the declared generation path.** With `--fixed-lengths 60 60`, MucOneUp draws each haplotype independently from its transition model, so two 60-repeat haplotypes are never sequence-identical. Identical haplotypes, non-X enrichment, interruptions, and long X runs all require `--input-structure` with authored chains. The maintained experiment schema has exactly seven fields and no structure input. Remedy: add a schema version 2 with an optional `structure` field, author structure files deterministically from `bio_seed`, validate them through the strict truth adapter, and label them as authored designs in the ledger, as the prompt requires for non-native features.

**C4, CRITICAL. Section 2.1, lines 36 to 41 and Section 5. The seed policy is not implementable by the current runner and has a documented collision.** The runner passes one `seed` to both `simulate` and `reads amplicon`. The three-seed policy needs the schema change from C3. Separately, `reads amplicon --seed S` derives pbsim3 seeds S+1 and S+2 for the two haplotypes and CCS seeds S+100·hap+bam. Consecutive base seeds across designs therefore share a pbsim3 seed, exactly the cross-contamination the review question asks about. Remedy: disjoint, non-overlapping ranges with stride ≥1000 for `bio_seed`, `hifi_seed`, and `ont_seed`; record the derived component seeds in the sealed ledger.

**M1, MAJOR. Section 2.1, line 36. The "sequencing error independence" claim is only half right, and the strong pairing property is not stated.** The `reads amplicon` seed controls pbsim3 error and CCS sampling. PCR allocation uses the closed-form deterministic split (stochastic mode off), so per-allele template counts are identical across platforms for a design. That is a pairing strength the spec should state, together with the requirement that `pcr_bias.stochastic` stays false. Also, the per-haplotype amplicon templates live in a temporary directory that is deleted; the existing pre-merge capture wrapper should be extended to retain the per-allele template counts and amplicon FASTA hashes so molecule-level truth is available for dev.

**M2, MAJOR. Section 2.3, "Extreme Asymmetry" and Section 3.2(2), line 110. Minority support is a deterministic function of length and template count, and the gate sits at its edge.** With the default PCR preset, expected minority templates at 200 requested are roughly: 25/140 about 5, 30/120 about 11, 25/100 about 16, 60/80 about 68. After the CCS filter (about 85% yield observed), 25/140 gives about 4 usable long reads, so the "≥5 spanning reads" condition will rarely hold and the stratum will be nearly empty at the medium and low tiers. Remedy: define the stratum by expected minority fraction computed from the PCR model and the actual primer positions, not by nominal lengths. Request templates for extreme designs to hit predeclared minority tiers (about 3, 6, 12 expected molecules). Include at least two designs with expected minority ≤3 to test the "insufficient evidence, no false second allele" contract. Report the unconditional rate alongside the conditional one, and measure "spanning" from captured source truth rather than caller anchors.

**M3, MAJOR. Section 3.1(4) and 3.2(1). "Confident normal negative" and the identical-stratum gate conflict with the codebase's evidence contract.** The pipeline explicitly refuses to declare homozygosity from absence of variants, and identical designs cannot be proven to be two alleles from amplicon reads. A 70% confident-negative target on a panel with identical designs either fails by construction or rewards weakening that contract. Remedy: define three negative outcomes: confident negative (two independently supported alleles, no mutation), single-sequence negative (one sequence, multiplicity unresolved, no mutation), unresolved. Set the gate on the first two combined and report identical designs separately. Reword 3.2(1) as "one length candidate, no false split, multiplicity status unresolved, no mutation".

**M4, MAJOR. Section 3.1(3), line 100. The FDR gate is undefined.** The evaluator distinguishes annotation extras (baseline 14) from supported extras (baseline 0). If "supported", the gate is already met; if "annotation", it demands a drop from 37% to 10%. State which, and define the denominator as records or samples.

**M5, MAJOR. Section 3.1(4), lines 102 to 104. Specificity numbers are internally inconsistent.** One false alarm across 22 dev controls is 95.5% and passes; one across 10 final controls is 90% and fails the same rule. "Zero tolerance" and "maximum 1" conflict. Remedy: zero new alarms relative to baseline on paired designs, plus an absolute cap expressed in counts per split.

**M6, MAJOR. Section 3.2(3), line 112. The gap-1 gate is fragile and underspecified.** Twenty designs across gaps 1, 2, 3 leave about five dev HiFi gap-1 designs; 100% means one failure fails the gate. "Coverage ≥30x" is undefined (per allele, usable reads, or spanning reads). Remedy: state the count (for example at least n-1 of n), define coverage as captured per-allele usable reads, and restrict the 100% form to HiFi since ONT per-read length noise at 0.95 accuracy makes gap-1 resolution doubtful.

**M7, MAJOR. Section 2.3, "Boundary Repeat Mutations". The definition is unrealizable as written.** Total-repeat indices 1 to 5 and the last four are fixed units. None of the 13 mutations is allowed on repeats 1 to 4 or 7 to 9; only delGCCCA is allowed on 5, 5C, 6, 6p. Remedy: define boundary as the first or last three canonical repeats (total indices 6 to 8 and L-6 to L-4), and add an explicit delGCCCA-on-fixed-repeat sub-stratum, which also stresses the ladder's constant region and the exact trimming anchors.

**M8, MAJOR. Section 2.3 table. Marginal counts do not form a design.** Length rows sum to 92, leaving 8 designs unassigned; "Length Extremes" and "Extreme Asymmetry" overlap. Remedy: publish the 100-row design table (lengths, structure source, mutation, haplotype, target index, template count, expected minority fraction, split) and the seeded stratified split procedure before generation. Note that with 13 types × 2 haplotypes and 20 final mutation designs, per-type sensitivity is unmeasurable in the final panel; say so.

**M9, MAJOR. Section 3, missing content. Evaluation and freeze protocol are not declared.** The evaluator already implements maximum-cardinality, minimum-Levenshtein one-to-one assignment with all optima reported. The spec must freeze that evaluator's hash, the tie rule, the paired analysis unit (design), the resampling scheme (design-level bootstrap preserving platform pairing), the caller source hash, settings hash, Clair3 model hashes, and tool versions. The fresh-generation driver already has a freeze-hash mechanism; reuse it.

**M10, MAJOR. Section 3, missing content. Final-panel power is too low for the stated confirmation.** For diploid-exact rising from about 23% to 38%, 30 HiFi designs give a Wilson interval of roughly 22% to 55% around 11/30, overlapping the baseline. Remedy: predeclare that final validation is a paired no-regression confirmation with intervals reported, not a significance test, and state the pass rule as "point estimate above baseline and at most k paired regressions".

**M11, MAJOR. Section 4, Family E, and Section 3. No inner selection split.** Factorial screening over 140 dev datasets with many candidate configurations will overfit. Remedy: grouped 5-fold cross-validation by design, or a fixed 50/20 tuning/selection split within dev, predeclared with the number of configurations to be screened.

**M12, MAJOR. Section 2.3 and 2.4. Partial reads, chimeras, and QNAME collisions are unaddressed.** MucOneUp has no chimera model, so say so in 2.4. Partial reads exist only as the documented deterministic clipping perturbation; label those as derivatives within the same split, outside the 200. Simulator read names collide and renaming changed results in the validation report. Declare which input is canonical (recommend uniquely renamed reads with the mapping sealed) so the choice is not a confound.

**M13, MAJOR. Section 2.3 coverage row. Tiers confound platform with yield and will be mostly no-calls at the low tier.** HiFi loses about 15% of templates to the CCS filter; ONT loses none. For 60/80 at 20 templates the longer allele gets about 6 usable HiFi reads, below `min_coverage` 10, so the baseline cannot call. Remedy: define tiers by realized usable reads per platform (bins predeclared), record realized counts in the sealed ledger, and state that the low tier primarily tests the no-call contract.

**MIN1, MINOR. Line 39. `bio_seed` does not control mutation placement.** Placement is explicit via `--mutation-targets`; the seed influences composition and any permissive parent conversion.

**MIN2, MINOR. Section 5, line 148. Statuses mix execution and scientific outcomes.** Add `ambiguous_reconstruction`, `no_call`, and `completed_inaccurate` as the prompt requires.

**MIN3, MINOR. Section 2.5. Pilot scope.** Add one extreme design at 200 templates and one low-tier design to verify realized yields, one `--input-structure` design if C3 is adopted, and a 13-entry diff of mutation definitions between simulator config and dictionary.

**MIN4, MINOR. Section 3.3. Runtime and RSS gates lack a measurement protocol.** Specify alternating paired runs, N≥5, median, same machine, and the excluded non-scientific fields for output equivalence. The 8 GB cap needs a measured baseline.

**ADV1, ADVISORY. ONT accuracy is not declared.** The maintained config uses QSHMM-ONT-HQ at mean accuracy 0.95, while the caller maps ONT with `lr:hq`, a preset intended for Q20+ reads. Declare the accuracy as a fixed stratum and treat results as model-specific.

## Independent brainstorming and architectural recommendations

**Family A, reference architecture.** The concrete defect is that the ladder uses the first 500 bases of the stored 10 kb left flank, while amplicon reads carry the last bases before the VNTR. Every read's left end is therefore soft-clipped and the left trimming anchor can never be biological. The fix is `flanking_left[-500:]` plus a check that the primer-to-VNTR distance from the MucOneUp config is covered. Risks: minimap2 chaining changes, trimming anchor coordinates move, and every projected mutation position and VCF-support replay must be re-validated. Discriminating experiment: on cached dev BAMs, compare distal versus proximal ladder on left soft-clip length distribution, anchor success rate, per-contig AS, length pairs, and exact sequences. On X-only versus composition: because non-X units differ from X by a few substitutions, composition shifts the AS baseline per haplotype, which mean-AS refinement conflates with length fit. Recommend "length first, composition second": keep the ladder only for coarse length, then build per-allele composition references. The most principled alternative is per-read unit decoding with a repeat-unit HMM (label each 60 bp unit), giving length and composition together; test decoding accuracy per read against dev truth structures on both platforms before investing further.

**Family B, iterative allele references.** Failure modes: minority collapse when the polished majority reference attracts minority reads; reinforcement of early homopolymer errors, worst on ONT; non-identifiability for equal lengths where two references converge; oscillation; coordinate drift breaking mutation projection. Formulation: hard EM with per-read log-likelihood ratios from explicit realignment to both references, a dominance margin δ, a per-reference floor of m uniquely dominant records, convergence when assignments change below ε, a maximum iteration count, and collapse to one reference with "multiplicity unresolved" when the floor fails. Cross-fit by splitting reads with a deterministic hash: build from half A, score assignment stability on half B. Discriminating experiments: 60/80 with 10% minority from captured source labels, tracking minority retention per iteration; 60/60 identical, expecting convergence to one sequence and no invented differences; 60/60 variant with a single mutation, expecting separation.

**Family C, length and molecule inference.** Three quantities must stay separate: candidate fit (a read can fit several lengths), independent support (distinct records, never QNAME), and molecule count (unknown). Do not rely on minimap2's primary flag; the audits show the correct contig can have zero primaries. Instead realign each read explicitly to a small candidate set of 2 to 6 lengths and count reads that dominate one candidate by margin. For span evidence use error-tolerant flank anchors (edit distance ≤k, platform-specific k) and a discrete one-versus-two-component test with a per-read noise model; HiFi can resolve 60 bp differences, ONT needs a coverage condition. Two decisive diagnostics first: (1) classify the 59-rounded reads in 60/60 by aligning them to their own truth haplotype in dev, since MucOneUp has no stutter model, so those reads are either anchor failures or simulator deletions and the remedy differs; (2) a length-implausibility rule for minorities, because four 8.4 kb spanning reads cannot arise from a 25-repeat molecule by error, so retain them as a low-support candidate with reconstruction withheld rather than dropping them under a global floor.

**Family D, consensus and phasing.** Never emit IUPAC; use haplotype-specific consensus on phased VCFs and mask uncovered bases as N. Require a single connected phase set covering all heterozygous sites, else output per-block haplotypes with explicit boundaries. The documented false event arose because a single length cluster was treated as containing both homologs and low-QUAL SNPs were promoted to a second allele; gate phase-informative sites on QUAL and allele-depth balance, and require realignment dominance of each haplotype's reads. Assign all reads with `whatshap haplotag` rather than the internal downsampled read list, which turned 30:2 into 14:1. For two-haplotype amplicon data a direct k=2 clustering of the read-by-site allele matrix is simpler than general MEC and gives all-read assignment. Rescue low-QUAL known-motif mutations only from per-haplotype pileup support at the projected position.

**Family E, parameter matrices.** Strongest idea: after read assignment each allele is haploid, so run Clair3 in `--haploid_precise` or `--haploid_sensitive` mode per allele; this removes the class of spurious heterozygous calls that feed false splits. Test it first with an oracle assignment from captured source labels to get the ceiling. minimap2: `--secondary=yes -N 20 -p 0.9` to expose more alternatives for fit scoring, `-r` and `-z` large enough that 60×Δ indels do not fracture chains, `map-ont` versus `lr:hq` at the declared 0.95 accuracy. WhatsHap: `--internal-downsampling`, `--mapping-quality`, `--error-rate`. Hold Clair3 model version, coverage, and pbsim3 model fixed within each contrast and use the inner split from M11. Add a small derivative stratum at a second ONT accuracy to detect overfitting to one error model.

**Family F, performance.** Profile first: after the bit-vector merge, Clair3 dominates. Candidates in order of expected payoff and risk: restrict Clair3 to the VNTR interval with a BED, reuse a hash-keyed ladder `.mmi` across samples, stream per-allele remapping instead of buffering FASTQ and SAM strings, compute contig counts from the SAM stream instead of a second idxstats pass, and budget threads across concurrent allele tasks. Gate every change on scientific-output equivalence with an explicit excluded-field list and alternating paired timings.

**Priority order for discriminating experiments:** (1) v0.11.0 baseline on all 140 dev datasets with a first-wrong-stage failure atlas; (2) oracle ceilings using truth read assignment and truth references in dev, to decide whether assignment, calling, or consensus is the binding constraint; (3) the proximal-flank ladder ablation on cached BAMs; (4) explicit-realignment dominance versus error-tolerant span versus current on the length endpoint across gap 0, 1, 2, 3 and asymmetry strata, HiFi and ONT separately; (5) haploid Clair3 per assigned allele with oracle assignment; (6) the 59-read stutter diagnostic.

Next step: revise the spec for C1 to C4 and M1 to M13, publish the 100-row design table and sealed split, extend the runner schema, then resubmit before the pilot.
